explain.say: Sometimes they say yes: say thank you, learn the rules, have fun. Sometimes not now: that is okay, try another game, or ask again later. Either way, you were brave! Your challenge: ask to join a game this week.

faq.q: What do I say to join a game?
faq.a: Walk close and say, Can I play too? or Can I join in? Say it clearly and smile if you can.
asks: Tell me about Can I play too?

faq.q: What if I feel shy about joining?
faq.a: Take a slow breath, and watch the game first. You can also ask a friend to come with you.
asks: Tell me about Ana wants to join

faq.a: Watching helps you learn the rules and see a good moment to ask, like between rounds.

faq.q: What if they say not now?
faq.a: That is okay. It does not mean they do not like you. Try another game, or ask again later. A grown-up you trust can help too.
asks: Tell me about They say not now

faq.q: How do the other children feel when I join?
faq.a: Often they are glad. More players can make the game more fun.

facts: Tag is a chasing game played by children in many countries.
Watching a game first helps you learn its rules before you join.

quiz.say: What can Ana say to join the game?
quiz.why: Can I play too? is a friendly way to ask.

wrong.1: Grabbing or demanding can upset others.
wrong.2: Unkind words make people not want to play.

quiz.say: They say not now. What can you do?
quiz.show: They say not now. What can you do?
quiz.why: Trying another game, or asking later, is calm and brave.

wrong.2: One not now is not forever. Try again.
